# dsh-pwsh-plugin
**English** · 简体中文
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-pwsh-plugin) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugi
(https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-pwsh-plugin) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
A `pwsh_run` tool for DeepSeek Harness: PowerShell script text goes to a **persistent** pwsh 7 proce

ss
over stdin, so nothing is escaped on the way in, there is no 32K command-line cap, the ~400 ms co

ld start
is paid once, and variables / location / modules survive from one call to the next.
It sits **next to** the built-in `pwsh` tool, it does not replace it.
The same repository also carries `wsl/llrun`, a small C shim that gives the `bash` tool a real write
boundary inside WSL. See docs/llrun.md.
The plugin page shows this package's own icon, its localized title and summary, and — in a Chinese U

I —
`README.zh-CN.md` rather than the English one. Each piece is declared where the harness looks fo

r it:
`icon.svg` through `package.json`'s `icon` field, and the text through `locale/en.json` plus
`
locale/zh.json` (only `meta.detail` can reach a document whose name is not literally `README`).
Requires **DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer** (tested on 0.2.0-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.3) and **PowerShell 7**.
## Why you want it
| Layer | What happens today |
| `bash` tool | Wraps the command as `/bin/bash -c "<cmd>"`. The outer double quotes expand `$` **be

fore** PowerShell ever sees it, and heredocs die in the same layer. |
| built-in `pwsh` tool | Passe
s `$` and here-strings through correctly, but each call is a brand-new process, and the whole comman

d rides the Windows command line: 32,000 characters is fine, 32,700 gives `spawn ENAMETOOLONG`. |
|
this tool | Script body travels as a base64 blob on stdin, so neither problem applies. |
Verified 91,741 characters in a single call. Full measurements and the reasoning behind every design
choice are in FINDINGS.md.
## Install
The package is a **DSH bundle**: it ships a `cordis.patch.yml` that inserts its own rows, so install

ing
it is all you do — you never edit your profile by hand.
It inserts two:

- `- id: pwsh-run` — the tool itself.
- `- id: custom-bash` — the `bash` tool replacement, Windows o

nly (`disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'`).
It points at `dsh-pwsh-plugin/wsl/custom-bash.m

js` inside the package, so the `llrun` binary that comes with
it is what the fence uses — nothing to

copy, nothing to install into `/usr/local/bin`. `remove` takes both
rows and the package away, leav
ing your profile exactly as it was.
It does **not** disable the stock `tool-bash`: that row already carries `disabled: !!js process.plat

form ===
'win32'`, and a hard `disabled: true` from here would switch the official bash off on Linux

===
'win32'`, and a hard `disabled: true` from here would switch the official bash off on Linux too.

## The tools
`pwsh_run` runs a script. Versions are managed by DSH itself — see Updating.
| Argument | Required | Meaning |
| `script` | yes | PowerShell script text. Reaches the server **verbatim** — do not escape `$`, do n

ot wrap it in `pwsh -c`, do not add outer quotes. |
| `workdir` | no | `Set-Location` first. The ses
sion is stateful, so later calls inherit it. An invalid path fails this call without running the scr

ipt. |
| `timeoutMs` | no | Per-call timeout, default 120000. |
Output: stdout as-is, warnings prefixed `WARNING: `, verbose prefixed `VERBOSE: `, a thrown exceptio

n
carries `[script threw]` plus the innermost message. Errors (`Write-Error`, a child process's stde

rr)
come **after** stdout — the server merges every stream through `*>&1` and tags lines by type, so
**line-by-line interleaving of stdout and stderr is not preserved** (the built-in tool keeps two co

lumns).
When order matters, merge them yourself: `2>&1` or `*>&1`.
## Configuration
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `pwshPath` | `pwsh` | Executable; resolved through `PATH` by default. |
| `timeoutMs` | `120000` |

Default per-call timeout. |
| `idleMs` | `1800000` | Recycle an idle session (30 minutes). |

## Known limitations
The full list — session semantics, detached child std handles, UAC differences, and what an update d

oes to a
session — lives in **docs/runtime-notes.md**. The short version:

- `read-only` mode is unsupported; use the built-in `pwsh` there.
- A timeout kills the whole sessio

n and reaps its child process tree.
- `exit N` codes and stdout/stderr interleaving are not observab

le.
- A session is serial, and there is no TTY.
- An update replaces the session; anything held only

is serial, and there is no TTY.
- An update replaces the session; anything held only in it is lost.
